title: Multi-system PATH safety (WSL/Cygwin) — share %PATH%
description:
WSL, Cygwin, and MSYS2 all share Windows %PATH% by default. Wanderlust's deduplication and dead-link removal affects PATH entries visible to these subsystems, which may have their own PATH-dependent state.

Needs:
- Understand each subsystem's PATH inheritance model
- Add probe that checks PATH sanity from WSL (wsl.exe echo $PATH)
- Consider subsystem-specific PATH sections or ignore lists

title: Cross-session persistence — track failures across runs
description:
Currently Wanderlust has no memory between healing cycles. Failures, rollbacks, and degraded states are not tracked across runs.

Needs:
- Persistent store for healing history (JSONL or SQLite in %LOCALAPPDATA%\wanderlust)
- Failure counters that escalate response (e.g., 3 consecutive failures → alert user)
- Trend analysis to detect degrading PATH quality before outright failure

title: AUTO mode heuristics — no ML/baselining
description:
Wanderlust's healing currently applies the same rules every cycle. There is no baselining of 'normal' PATH state per machine.

Needs:
- Learn typical PATH length, entry patterns, and frequency per machine
- Detect anomalies (unusual additions/removals) vs known-good baseline
- Configurable sensitivity: conservative (only fix dead links) vs aggressive (enforce baseline)

title: YANK detection from PATH — no grace period before healing
description:
If a USB drive or network share is temporarily disconnected, its PATH entry becomes a dead link. Wanderlust removes it immediately on next heal. When the drive reconnects, the entry is gone.

Needs:
- Grace period: mark entries as 'suspicious' instead of immediately removing
- Track disconnection events across heal cycles
- Only remove entries that have been missing for N consecutive cycles (configurable, default 3)
- Restore entries that reappear within the grace period

title: Planned backups — no integrity checks or partial-restore
description:
Backups are written as .reg files but never validated. A corrupted backup is worse than no backup — it creates false confidence.

Needs:
- Backup integrity checksum (SHA-256 of backed-up PATH)
- Restore dry-run mode (show what will change before applying)
- Partial restore (restore specific entries, not full overwrite)
- Backup rotation (keep last N successful backups)

title: Registry source of truth — no cross-ref with known-good state
description:
Healing decisions are based entirely on current registry state. There is no cross-reference with known-good states from different points in time.

Needs:
- Store periodic snapshots of 'healthy PATH' (e.g., after a successful heal + probe)
- Diff current PATH against last healthy snapshot
- Detect drift beyond threshold before it causes failures
- Rollback to last known-good snapshot on probe failure

title: Uninstall healing — no post-uninstall PATH check
description:
Wanderlust does not watch for software uninstall events. When a program is removed, its PATH entries remain orphaned until the next scheduled heal (up to 30 min later).

Needs:
- Optionally hook Windows Installer / AppX uninstall events
- React to WM_SETTINGCHANGE for immediate scan
- At minimum: improve detection of stale entries in registry uninstaller data

title: Logging depth — no structured logs, just debug!
description:
Current logging uses eprintln! and debug!. No structured logging at all.

Needs:
- Structured log format (JSON lines to file in %LOCALAPPDATA%\wanderlust\logs)
- Log levels: trace (full registry diff), info (heal summary), warn (degraded state), error (failure)
- Log rotation (max 10 MB per file, keep last 5)
- Optional: Windows Event Log integration for admin visibility

title: Registry backup last-write-wins race — no file-level mutex
description:
If two Wanderlust instances run simultaneously (e.g., overlapping scheduled tasks), both write PATH and backup .reg files concurrently. Last write wins, but there is no file-level mutex or advisory lock.

Needs:
- Mutex or lock file in %LOCALAPPDATA%\wanderlust to serialize writes
- Atomic write-and-verify protocol
- Stale lock detection with timeout (5 min)
